{{Short description|People with a net worth of at least US$1 million}}
[[File:Global billionaires.png|thumb|400x400px|The [[United States]], [[China]], and [[India]] lead the worldwide distribution of high-net-worth individuals, as of 2017.]]
In the [[financial services]] industry, a '''high-net-worth individual''' ('''HNWI''') is a person who maintains [[Market liquidity|liquid assets]] at or above a certain threshold. Typically the criterion is that the person's financial assets (excluding their [[primary residence]]) are valued [[Millionaire|over US$1{{nbsp}}million]].<ref name="investopedia.com">{{cite web|author=Investopedia Staff|date=19 April 2020|title=High-Net-Worth Individual (HNWI)|url=http://www.investopedia.com/terms/h/hnwi.asp|access-date=2020-11-10|website=Investopedia|archive-date=2006-05-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060523165038/http://www.investopedia.com/terms/h/hnwi.asp|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=World Wealth Report 2020 |url=https://www.capgemini.com/nl-nl/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2020/07/World-Wealth-Report-WWR-2020.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201110194206/https://www.capgemini.com/nl-nl/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2020/07/World-Wealth-Report-WWR-2020.pdf |archive-date=2020-11-10 |access-date=2020-11-09 |website=Capgemini}}</ref> A secondary level, a '''very-high-net-worth individual''' ('''VHNWI'''), is someone with at least US$5{{nbsp}}million in investable assets.<ref name="investopedia.com" /> The terminal level, an '''ultra-high-net-worth''' '''individual''' ('''UHNWI'''), holds at least US$30{{nbsp}}million in investable assets ([[Real and nominal value|adjusted for inflation]]).<ref name="auto">{{cite journal|last=Grzeskiewiecz|first=Grzegorz|author2=Tomasz Kozlinski|title=High Net Worth Individuals: The Clients of Private Banking|journal=8th International Conference of Doctoral Students|date=15–17 June 2004|volume=Brno University of Technology|issue=Czech Republic|url=http://www.privatebanking.pl/pdf/grzeskiewicz-kozlinski.pdf|access-date=6 March 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120324090219/http://www.privatebanking.pl/pdf/grzeskiewicz-kozlinski.pdf|archive-date=24 March 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> Individuals with a net worth of [[Billionaire|over US$1{{nbsp}}billion]] are considered to occupy a special bracket of the UHNWI.<ref name=":1" /><ref name="Joby Waite">{{Cite news |last1=Neate |first1=Rupert |date=2022-09-20 |title=Number of global ultra high net worth individuals hits record high |url=https://www.theguardian.com/news/2022/sep/20/number-global-ultra-high-net-worth-individuals-record-high |access-date=2023-03-05 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077 |archive-date=2023-03-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230305081655/https://www.theguardian.com/news/2022/sep/20/number-global-ultra-high-net-worth-individuals-record-high |url-status=live }}</ref> These thresholds are broadly used in studies of [[Distribution of wealth|wealth inequality]], government regulation, investment suitability requirements, marketing, financing standards, and general corporate strategy.

UHNWIs constitute only 0.003% of the world's population, yet hold 13% of the world's total wealth.{{cn|date=June 2026}} In 2017, 226,450 people were designated as UHNWI, with their combined total wealth increasing to $27{{nbsp}}trillion.<ref name="wealthx_2017_report">{{cite news |url=https://www.wealthx.com/report/exclusive-uhnwi-analysis-the-world-ultra-wealth-report-2017/ |series=Exclusive UHNWI Analysis |title=The World Ultra Wealth Report 2017 |edition=5 |date=June 27, 2017 |access-date=November 12, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171116204118/https://www.wealthx.com/report/exclusive-uhnwi-analysis-the-world-ultra-wealth-report-2017/ |archive-date=November 16, 2017 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

== United States: SEC regulations ==
{{See also|Accredited investor}}

The [[U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission]] requires all SEC-registered investment advisers to periodically file a report known as Form ADV.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sec.gov/answers/formadv.htm|title=SEC.gov - Form ADV|website=www.sec.gov|access-date=2017-08-29|archive-date=2016-12-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161223012336/https://www.sec.gov/answers/formadv.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> Form ADV requires each investment adviser to state how many of their clients are "high-net-worth individuals", among other details; its Glossary of Terms explains that a "high-net-worth individual" is a person who is either a "qualified client" under rule 205-3 of the Advisers Act (currently{{As of?|date=January 2026}} a person with at least $1,100,000 managed by the reporting investment adviser, or whose net worth the investment adviser reasonably believes exceeds $2,200,000 without counting their primary residence) or who is a "qualified purchaser" as defined in section 2(a)(51)(A) of the [[Investment Company Act of 1940]]. The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform Act mandates that the definition of a qualified client be reviewed every five years and adjusted for inflation.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Order Approving Adjustment for Inflation of the Dollar Amount Tests in Rule 205-3 Under the Investment Advisers Act.|url=https://www.sec.gov/rules/other/2021/ia-5756.pdf|access-date=2021-10-12|website=SEC.gov / Securities and Exchange Commission|language=en|archive-date=2021-08-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210806012756/https://www.sec.gov/rules/other/2021/ia-5756.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref> For SEC purposes, a person's net worth may include assets held jointly with their spouse. Unlike the definitions used in the financial and banking trade, the SEC's definition of HNWI includes the value of a person's verifiable non-financial assets, such as a primary residence or art collection.<ref>{{Cite web|title=17 CFR § 230.501 - Definitions and terms used in Regulation D.|url=https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/17/230.501|access-date=2020-11-10|website=LII / Legal Information Institute|language=en|archive-date=2021-04-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210414064148/https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/17/230.501|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Annual World Wealth Report ==
The World Wealth Report was co-published by [[Merrill Lynch]] and [[Capgemini]] who worked together since 1993, investigating the "needs of high-net-worth individuals" to "successfully serve this market segment". Their first annual World Wealth Report was published in 1996.<ref name="Capgemini2003">{{cite report|url=http://ml.com/media/14076.pdf |year=2003 |publisher=Capgemini |title=2003 World Wealth Report |access-date=10 September 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100102085510/http://ml.com/media/14076.pdf |archive-date=January 2, 2010 }}</ref> The World Wealth Report defines HNWIs as those who hold at least US$1{{nbsp}}million in assets excluding primary residence and UHNWIs as those who hold at least US$30{{nbsp}}million in assets excluding primary residence.<ref name="Capgemini2009-1">{{cite report|url=http://www.capgemini.com/resources/thought_leadership/2009_world_wealth_report|title=2009 World Wealth Report|publisher=Capgemini|year=2009|series=Thought Leadership|access-date=2009-07-07|archive-date=2017-07-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170710085815/https://www.capgemini.com/resources/thought_leadership/2009_world_wealth_report|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The report states that in 2008 there were 8.6{{nbsp}}million HNWIs worldwide, a decline of 14.9% from 2007. The total HNWI [[wealth]] worldwide totaled US$32.8{{nbsp}}trillion, a 19.5% decrease from 2007. The UHNWIs experienced the greater loss, losing 24.6% in population and 23.9% in accumulated wealth. The report revised its 2007 projections that HNWI financial wealth would reach US$59.1{{nbsp}}trillion by 2012 and revised this downward to a 2013 HNWI wealth valued at $48.5{{nbsp}}trillion advancing at an annual rate of 8.1%.<ref name="Capgemini2009-1" /> The "World Ultra Wealth Report", on UHNW populations—those with "$30m or more in net worth"—which was published on June 27, 2017, "this year revealed global growth of 3.5% to 226,450 individuals and a 1.5% increase of their total combined wealth to $27{{nbsp}}trillion."<ref name="wealthx_2017_report" />

The 2018 World Wealth Report<ref name="worldwealthreport.com">{{cite web |url=https://worldwealthreport.com/ |title=World Wealth Report |access-date=2019-12-27 |archive-date=2021-04-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210416191124/https://worldwealthreport.com/ |url-status=live }}</ref> was jointly produced by Capgemini and [[RBC Wealth Management]] and included, for the first time, the Global HNW Insights Survey produced in collaboration with Scorpio Partnership.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.scorpiopartnership.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010417004808/http://www.scorpiopartnership.com/ |archive-date=2001-04-17 |title=The Scorpio Partnership}}</ref> The inaugural survey represented one of the largest and most in-depth surveys of HNWIs ever conducted, surveying more than 4,400 across 21 major wealth markets in North America, Latin America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Middle East, and Africa.{{Table alignment}}

== Markets ==

Certain products cater to the wealthy, whose [[conspicuous consumption]] of [[luxury goods]] and services includes, such as: [[mansion]]s, [[yacht]]s, first-class airline tickets and [[Business jet|private jets]], and personal [[umbrella insurance]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://aeon.co/ideas/conspicuous-consumption-is-over-its-all-about-intangibles-now|title=Conspicuous consumption is over. It's all about intangibles now|author=Currid-Halkett, Elizabeth|website=Aeon Ideaslanguage=en|access-date=2018-12-24|archive-date=2021-04-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210416174819/https://aeon.co/ideas/conspicuous-consumption-is-over-its-all-about-intangibles-now|url-status=live}}</ref> As economic growth has made historically expensive items affordable for the middle-class, purchases have trended towards intangible products such as education.<ref name=":0" /> In the United States, [[concierge medicine]] is an emerging trend as of 2017.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/06/03/business/economy/high-end-medical-care.html|title=The Doctor Is In. Co-Pay? $40,000.|last=Schwartz|first=Nelson D.|date=2017-06-03|work=The New York Times|access-date=2018-12-24|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331|archive-date=2021-05-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210525015909/https://www.nytimes.com/2017/06/03/business/economy/high-end-medical-care.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Banking and finance ===
{{Main|Private banking|Wealth management}}

Most global banks, such as [[Barclays]], [[BNP Paribas]], [[Citibank]], [[Deutsche Bank]], [[HSBC]], [[JPMorgan Chase]], and [[UBS]], have a separate business unit with designated teams consisting of client advisors and product specialists exclusively for UHNWI. These clients are often considered to have characteristics similar to [[institutional investors]] because the vast majority of their net worth and current income is derived from [[Passive income|passive sources]] rather than [[Job (role)|labor]]. By 2006, asset managers working for HNW individuals invested more than £300{{nbsp}}billion on behalf of their clients. These wealth managers are bankers who in 2006, earned multimillion-pound salaries and owned their own companies and equity funds.<ref name="RivkinTimes2006">{{cite news|url=https://www.thetimes.com/business-money/companies/article/how-i-make-the-rich-richer-n8xbm2lg05c|date=12 December 2006|title=How I make the rich richer|first=Annabel|last=Rivkin|work=[[The Times]]|access-date=10 September 2013|location=London|archive-date=4 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250404193445/https://www.thetimes.com/business-money/companies/article/how-i-make-the-rich-richer-n8xbm2lg05c|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2006, a list of the 50 top investment bankers was published by the [[Spear's Wealth Management Survey]].

=== Other ===
{{See also|Offshore bank}}
Certain magazines, such as ''[[Monocle (UK magazine)|Monocle]]'',<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2017/nov/11/monocle-magazine-apartment-tyler-brule|title=Wealth: ''Monocle'': you've seen the magazine – now buy the apartment|author=Neate, Rupert|date=November 11, 2017|work=The Guardian|access-date=2018-12-24|language=en-GB|issn=0261-3077|archive-date=2021-04-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210416195258/https://www.theguardian.com/business/2017/nov/11/monocle-magazine-apartment-tyler-brule|url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[Robb Report]]'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nypost.com/2014/12/08/magazines-for-the-mega-rich/|title=Magazines for the mega-rich|author=Post Staff Report|date=December 8, 2014|work=New York Post|language=en|access-date=2018-12-24|archive-date=2021-04-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210416181739/https://nypost.com/2014/12/08/magazines-for-the-mega-rich/|url-status=live}}</ref> and ''[[Worth (magazine)|Worth]]'', are designed for a high net worth audience. By 2012, according to ''Reuters'', the UHNW individuals held $32{{nbsp}}trillion in offshore havens, representing $280{{nbsp}}billion in lost income tax revenues.<ref name="Reuters_20120722">{{Cite news| title = Super rich hold $32{{nbsp}}trillion in offshore havens| work = Reuters| access-date = 22 April 2020| date = July 22, 2012| url = https://www.reuters.com/article/us-offshore-wealth-idUSBRE86L03U20120722| archive-date = 11 April 2020| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200411075902/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-offshore-wealth-idUSBRE86L03U20120722| url-status = live}}</ref> Brands in various sectors, such as [[Bentley]], [[Maybach]], and [[Rolls-Royce Motor Cars|Rolls-Royce]] actively target UHNWI and HNWI to sell their products. In 2006, Rolls-Royce researchers suggested there were 80,000 people in ultra-high-net-worth category around the world. UHNW individuals "have, on average, eight cars and three or four homes. Three-quarters own a jet aircraft and most have a yacht."<ref name="HuttonTimes5nov2006">{{cite news |author=Ray Hutton |author-link=Jewels in the Crown#About the author |date=5 November 2006 |title=Rich spurn ultra-luxury cars |url=http://www.thesundaytimes.co.uk/sto/business/article40905.ece |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222152116/http://www.thesundaytimes.co.uk/sto/business/article40905.ece |archive-date=February 22, 2014 |access-date=10 September 2013 |publisher=The Sunday Times |location=UK}}</ref>

The [[Boston Consulting Group]] (BCG) 2014 Global Wealth Report<ref name="BCG_2014">{{cite web|url=https://www.bcg.com/publications/2014/financial-institutions-business-unit-strategy-global-wealth-2014-riding-wave-growth.aspx|title=Global Wealth 2014: Riding a Wave of Growth|website=www.bcg.com|access-date=2018-08-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180808111934/https://www.bcg.com/publications/2014/financial-institutions-business-unit-strategy-global-wealth-2014-riding-wave-growth.aspx|archive-date=2018-08-08|url-status=live}}</ref> shows that liquid wealth of the super-rich, referenced as Ultra-High-Net-Worth households, had increased by 20% in 2013. BCG uses a household definition of UHNW, which places only those with more than $100{{nbsp}}million liquid financial wealth into the UHNW-category, more than the usual $30{{nbsp}}million, with which the ultra-category had been created in 2007. They control 5.5% of global financial wealth. 5,000 of them live in the US, followed by China, Britain and Germany. BCG expects the trend toward more concentrated wealth to continue unabated. While financial wealth of the sub-millionaires is expected to increase by 3.7% annually until 2019, the expected growth rate for the super-rich is 9.1%.

67.7% of the world's UHNW population was self-made, 8.5% have fully inherited their wealth and 23.7% have both inherited and self-made wealth according to a 2018 report.<ref name="d358">{{cite web | last=Clifford | first=Catherine | title=Nearly 68% of the world's richest people are 'self-made,' says new report | website=CNBC | date=26 September 2019 | url=https://www.cnbc.com/2019/09/26/majority-of-the-worlds-richest-people-are-self-made-says-new-report.html | access-date=19 July 2025}}</ref> According to the same report, twenty-three percent of self-made UHNW individuals have derived their wealth in finance, banking and investment, 8.5 percent in consumer and business services and 7.6 percent in real estate. The share of inherited and self-made wealth varied by country.<ref name="s808">{{cite web | last=Ingraham | first=Christopher | title=People like the estate tax a whole lot more when they learn how wealth is distributed | website=The Washington Post | date=6 February 2019 | url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/us-policy/2019/02/06/people-like-estate-tax-whole-lot-more-when-they-learn-how-wealth-is-distributed/ | access-date=19 July 2025 | archive-date=20 August 2025 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250820073255/https://www.washingtonpost.com/us-policy/2019/02/06/people-like-estate-tax-whole-lot-more-when-they-learn-how-wealth-is-distributed/ | url-status=live }}</ref>

==UHNWI role in economies ==
{{See also|High-net-worth individual#Markets}}
UHNWIs are notable players in the field of philanthropy; many have their own private foundations and support a variety of causes, from education to poverty relief. Financial institutions are known for their targeting of UHNWIs, having specific parts of their bank designed to manage the wealth of their UHNW clients.<ref name="auto"/> In addition, research on the UHNW is particularly important with upcoming intergenerational wealth transfers in the UHNW population.<ref name="cfainstitute_2014">{{cite web|last=Foster|first=Lauren|title=Why Financial Advisers Need to Use Social Media|date=5 February 2014 |url=https://blogs.cfainstitute.org/investor/2014/02/05/why-financial-advisers-need-to-use-social-media/|access-date=2024-11-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140306083611/http://blogs.cfainstitute.org/investor/2014/02/05/why-financial-advisers-need-to-use-social-media/|archive-date=2014-03-06|url-status=live}}</ref> For example, as of 2014, luxury companies typically target UHNW as a separate segment of their clientele. ''Daily Finance'' in 2014, projected that growth in Asia's UHNW population looked promising for the future of the luxury industry.<ref>{{cite news|last=Kelesidou|first=Fani|title=Why High-End Luxury Brands Are Losing Their Luster|url=http://www.dailyfinance.com/2014/03/05/why-high-end-luxury-brands-could-start-losing-thei/|newspaper=Daily Finance|date=5 March 2014|access-date=6 March 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140306090721/http://www.dailyfinance.com/2014/03/05/why-high-end-luxury-brands-could-start-losing-thei/|archive-date=6 March 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The India's ''Economic Times'' said in 2014 that, despite the luxury industry's troubled year with China's luxury spenders, luxury industry experts continued to be optimistic for their long-term performance, especially from UHNWIs.<ref>{{cite news|last=PTI|title=Luxury industry optimistic about January–March quarter: Wealth-X survey|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/cons-products/fashion-/-cosmetics-/-jewellery/luxury-industry-optimistic-about-january-march-quarter-wealth-x-survey/articleshow/31477208.cms|newspaper=India Times: Economic Times|date=5 March 2014|access-date=9 November 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170207095540/http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/news-by-industry/cons-products/fashion-/-cosmetics-/-jewellery/luxury-industry-optimistic-about-january-march-quarter-wealth-x-survey/articleshow/31477208.cms|archive-date=7 February 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> According to Savills and Wealth-X, in 2014, UHNWIs are particularly relevant to the real estate sector, with the total UHNW population's [[real estate]] holdings accounting for over US$5{{nbsp}}trillion by 2014, or 3% of the world's real estate holdings. This is a huge proportion considering this population is only 0.003% of the world's population.<ref>{{cite book|last=Savills and Wealth-X|title=Around the World in Dollars and Cents|year=2014|page=2|url=https://pdf.euro.savills.co.uk/residential---other/private-wealth.pdf|access-date=2024-11-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140514114222/http://pdf.euro.savills.co.uk/residential---other/private-wealth.pdf|archive-date=2014-05-14|url-status=live}}</ref>
